summary: This work extends a 1D spin-qubit shuttling bus architecture optimized for syndrome extraction to support transversal two-qubit logical gates via pairwise interactions between data qubits from distant logical elements, with all-to-all connectivity and logical error rates reaching $2 \times 10^{-10}$ per syndrome-extraction round at distance $d=21$. The architecture integrates ancilla-sharing schemes to compress the physical footprint, explores 2D junction-based connectivity to reduce inter-qubit distances, and demonstrates application to 15-to-1 magic state distillation with optimized logical-qubit placement via Quantum Reverse Mapping.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires both reliable error-corrected qubit storage and high-fidelity logical operations between separated patches; existing work focuses on either syndrome extraction or isolated two-qubit gates, leaving the co-design of storage and transversal computation largely unexplored.
method: Building on the Quantum Reverse Mapping methodology from Escofet et al. (2026), the authors concatenate optimized logical elements along a single shuttling bus, benchmark memory and transversal CNOT logical error rates under a realistic spin-qubit noise model including gate depolarization, dephasing ($T_\phi^\mathrm{Store}$ and $T_\phi^\mathrm{Op}$), and distance-dependent shuttling dephasing, and explore architectural tradeoffs including symmetric versus asymmetric shuttling, ancilla-sharing ratios $m \in \{1,2,4,6,8\}$, and 1D versus 2D topologies.
result: Symmetric shuttling improves transversal CNOT fidelity by up to 60% at large code distances; ancilla sharing with $m=2$ outperforms the $m=1$ baseline beyond $\sim 14$ logical hops; 2D grid connectivity reduces worst-case logical-hop separations from $\mathcal{O}(N)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{N})$ with consistent improvements across all code distances; the 15-to-1 magic state distillation circuit achieves estimated distillation failure probability below $10^{-3}$ at $d=15$ with $T_\phi^\mathrm{Store}=800$ µs.
